line: e3 Nf6 d3 e5 a3 d5 h3 Bd6 b3 O-O g3 c6 Bb2
teaches: A slow setup with pawns on the third rank is answered on its own terms: build the same shape, then develop the bishop onto the diagonal where the opponent's centre pawn already stands. The bishop arrives with a target rather than into empty space, which is the whole difference between a passive system and a patient one.
explains: Both sides have made modest pawn moves and the position is still closed. The bishop goes to b2 on the long diagonal, where it hits the pawn on e5 and covers d4 — the square the centre would be contested from. It also holds the rook in the corner. Nothing has been risked, and the piece that will decide the game is pointing at the only fixed target on the board.
